subject: Secure shadow routing + cert chain orchestration for private endpoints

To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: netops@acme-finance.com
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Secure shadow routing + cert chain orchestration for private endpoints

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking a look. We're standing up a private Redwood deployment in our AWS VPC and have a few constraints that make the standard ACME-sidecar flow tricky:

- Several on-prem customers will route traffic through our transit VPC and then through an internal edge proxy (no public FQDN for some tenants).
- We need mutual TLS for east-west requests plus client cert pinning for a handful of legacy clients.
- Our security team requires rotation windows <= 30 days for leaf certs and wants the CA chain anchored to our offline root (we can publish an intermediate).

Questions we have:
1) Best way to manage short-lived leaf certs when the edge proxy doesn't have a routable public FQDN? Can we rely on internal ACME with DNS challenges or do you recommend CSR delegation?
2) How would Redwood's runtime handle OCSP/CRL checks for an internal-only chain (no public OCSP responder)?
3) Any gotchas with SNI mapping when we shadow-route tenant FQDNs inside the VPC (we're worried about SNI collisions and wildcard fallthroughs)?

I've attached an updated network diagram (network-diagram-v2.pdf) and a sample on-prem CSR that our PKI team produced.

We'd like a short design review with your infra and security folks tomorrow if possible.

Thanks,

Priya Raman
Head of Infrastructure
Acme Finance

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: Priya Raman <priya.r@acme-finance.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Secure shadow routing + cert chain orchestration for private endpoints

Priya —

Thanks for the detail and the diagram. High level thoughts before the design call:

- Internal ACME + DNS challenge: works if you can reliably update the private DNS zone used by the edge. If your VPC-hosted resolver is authoritative for the tenant namespace, ACME DNS challenges handled by an automated DNS hook are the cleanest path for short-lived certs.

- CSR delegation: recommended when the proxy is air-gapped or cannot be reached for any challenge. Redwood supports a CSR handoff flow where the customer's PKI issues the leaf and we accept an intermediate-signed chain. That fits the offline root requirement.

- OCSP/CRL: if you cannot provide a public OCSP responder, we suggest running an internal OCSP responder reachable from the Redwood runtime or use stapling at the proxy layer. For maximum reliability, publish an internal OCSP responder behind the VPC resolver and configure Redwood's cert verifier to query it. We can also disable live OCSP checks and rely on short-lived certs + revocation windows if your policy allows it.

- SNI shadowing: common pattern is to canonicalize tenant-host mappings and enumerate exact SNI entries per proxy. Avoid relying on wildcard fallthrough for multi-tenant hosts — explicit mapping reduces risk. For load-balanced edge pools, ensure the SNI mapping and upstream SNI forwarded header are preserved so the runtime can route to the correct model host.

Action items I propose for the call:
1) Confirm which tenant namespaces are public vs. private (list).
2) Decide on ACME automation vs. CSR delegation for each namespace.
3) Identify an internal OCSP/CRL plan (responder vs stapling vs short-lived-only).
4) Share a SNI mapping export and current edge proxy config (we can iterate).

I attached a quick checklist I use for private handoffs (redwood-private-cert-checklist.xlsx).

Available 1–3pm PT tomorrow — let me know what works and I'll send a calendar invite.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Principal Infra PM, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-12T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Secure shadow routing + cert chain orchestration for private endpoints

Hannah — forwarding Priya's thread and your reply. A couple internal notes before the call:

On ACME vs CSR delegation:
- If Acme Finance cannot automate private DNS changes (some of their tenants are managed by on-prem teams), we'll need a hybrid approach: ACME for the VPC-owned zones, CSR delegation for on-prem-only zones.

On OCSP and stapling:
- We should prototype stapling at the edge proxy first; that avoids exposing an internal OCSP responder across many subnets. Redwood's runtime already supports cached stapled responses for upstream certs (we implemented this in the 2026 tokenization rollout). Need to validate TTL behavior with their revocation policy.

On SNI mapping and routing safety:
- Karthik: can you prepare a short checklist for SNI collision detection and a script to expand exact-match rules from their tenant list?
- Neha: please draft a minimal RBAC model for who can request CSR handoffs and who can push cert bundles into the runtime. This needs to be auditable for their SOC 2 reviewer.

I'll take the call notes and consolidate into a design doc.

On attachments: see the sample CSR Priya sent (acme-onprem-csr-sample.txt) — their CSR uses a SAN list with multiple tenant entries which could complicate rotate flows.

Thanks — Marissa

Hannah / team —

Thanks — 2pm PT tomorrow works for us. We've pulled the tenant namespace list and flagged three that are fully on-prem (no private DNS automation). For those, we'll plan CSR delegation. For the rest, we'll try to automate DNS updates and use internal ACME with DNS challenge.

A couple clarifications before the call:
- We'll publish an intermediate CA (signed by our offline root) and can host an internal OCSP responder in the transit VPC.
- For older clients that require client cert pinning, we'll issue client certs from a dedicated intermediate with a 30-day rotation window.

Next steps:
1) Please send a calendar invite for 2026-10-14 14:00 PT and include a short agenda.
2) Karthik, Marissa, Neha — if you can bring the SNI checklist and RBAC draft that Marissa outlined, that would be great.

Attaching the sample CSR again.

Best,
